title: English gymnast Gabriel Langton suffers serious head and neck injury at Commonwealth Games
dek: Gabriel Langton, 18, fell off the high bar during England's men's team gymnastics final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, landing on his head and neck. He was treated at the arena, placed in a neck brace, and transported to hospital. Team officials reported he was moving and speaking to doctors.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Langton fell off the high bar after missing a grab midway through his routine and landed on his head and neck, requiring immediate medical attention and hospitalization.
bottom_line: Langton's condition and full extent of injuries remain unreported as of Friday evening. The next official update from the English team or hospital will shape understanding of his prognosis and timeline.
body: An 18-year-old English gymnast sustained a serious head and neck injury during the men's team gymnastics final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Friday, forcing immediate medical intervention and hospitalization.

Gabriel Langton fell off the high bar after missing a grab midway through his routine, according to ESPN's reporting. He landed on his head and neck and received extensive treatment at the arena before being transported on a stretcher in a neck brace.

Team officials said Langton was moving and speaking to doctors during initial treatment. A team spokesperson confirmed he was taken to hospital and stated, "We will share more information when it is available," without providing further detail on the nature or severity of his injuries.

The incident occurred during England's team final. Despite the injury overshadowing the competition, England's men's team secured silver with a final score of 238.20 points, according to ESPN. Canada won gold with 241.400 points, marking the first time England has failed to claim team gold at the Commonwealth Games since the Delhi Games in 2010, per ESPN's reporting. Scotland placed third and Australia completed the podium with 235.650 points.

Langton had replaced Olympic medallist Max Whitlock in the team earlier in the month, assuming a prominent role in the lineup. Luke Whitehouse, 24, followed Langton on the high bar and scored 11.70. The English team also included three-time European champion Whitehouse, Adam Tobin, Alex Yolshin-Cash, and Josh Nathan. Whitehouse posted the top score of the competition on floor, while Yolshin-Cash delivered the best parallel bars routine, per ESPN.

Canada's team was led by Felix Dolci, who scored highest on both vault and high bar, according to ESPN. In individual apparatus qualifying, Northern Ireland's Rhys McClenaghan placed third on pommel, behind Scotland's Reuben Ward and Jordan Carroll of Canada.

The specific nature and severity of Langton's injuries have not been disclosed. His recovery timeline and return-to-competition status remain unknown pending further information from team medical staff.
